transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… people have been telling me I’m hard to follow. At work, someone asks something simple, like when a ring repair will be done, and I start answering but somehow I’m talking about invoices, then garden soil, then mortgage papers. I can see them kind of losing me. That’s why I came in.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected or jumping from one idea to another when this happens?

Yes… I think so. It’s like I start with the answer, but then it slips off into other things—like invoices, or something about garden soil, or mortgage papers. I don’t really mean to. People just… stop following.
Do you ever think that there's something unusual or unreal going on that other people don't seem to notice?

I… maybe. I know it probably sounds strange, but sometimes I get the feeling certain customers aren’t really there for jewelry. Like they’re checking up on whether I’ll miss payments or something, because they ask so many questions about the new showroom. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but… I don’t know.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people don't?

Sometimes. When the shop is quiet, I’ll hear… like a woman muttering my name from the polishing room. Or I smell burning metal even when the torches are off. I usually go check, because it feels real enough.
Do you think the voice you hear calling your name is real?
At the time, yes… or close enough that I go look. I know later it might not make sense, but when I hear my name from the polishing room, it feels real.
Do you find it difficult to stay on topic in conversations, even when you're not feeling stressed or anxious?

Yes… I think so. It’s embarrassing. Someone asks me something simple at the shop, like when a ring repair will be ready, and I start answering but then I’m talking about invoices, or the garden soil, or the mortgage papers. I can see them getting confused, so I try to stop.
Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized than your speech, or is it the other way around?

I’m not sure I can separate them. It feels like the thoughts get tangled first, and then it comes out that way. Like I said… someone asks when a ring repair will be ready, and suddenly I’m talking about invoices, garden soil, mortgage papers. Then I see I’ve lost them.
Do you believe that people are actually checking up on you or plotting against you when they ask questions about the new showroom?

I… yes, sometimes I do think that. I know it probably sounds odd, but when customers keep asking about the new showroom, I get convinced they’re really checking whether I’m going to miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but it doesn’t always feel that way to me.
Do you hold any strong beliefs that you think are true, even when others tell you they are not?

Yes… I suppose so. I know it sounds odd, but when certain customers ask too much about the new showroom, I get convinced they’re really checking whether I’ll miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but I don’t always believe that.
Do you think these beliefs about people checking up on you are part of a larger plan or scheme?

I don’t know if I’d call it a whole scheme. It’s more… I get convinced some customers are coming in just to check on whether I’ll miss payments, because they keep asking about the new showroom. Even when my husband says they’re only being friendly, it doesn’t always feel that way.
Do you think these beliefs about people checking up on you are something you think about all the time, or just sometimes?

Just sometimes. It’s not every minute or anything… but when they start asking too much about the new showroom, I can get stuck on it and think they’re really checking if I’ll miss payments. Even if my husband says they’re just being friendly.
Do you hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear when you're not alone or in a quiet place?

Sometimes, yes. When the shop is quiet, I’ll hear… like a woman muttering my name from the polishing room. Or I’ll smell burning metal even when the torches are off. I usually go check, because it feels real at the time.
Do you believe these people checking up on you are part of an organized group or is it just individual customers?

I don’t think it’s, like, an organized group. It feels more like certain customers… asking too much about the new showroom, like they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments. I know that sounds odd.
Do you think these beliefs about people checking up on you are all connected in some way?

Kind of, yes. I know it sounds strange, but when certain customers keep asking about the new showroom, it all feels connected… like they’re really checking whether I’m going to miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but I still get convinced sometimes.
Do you think there's one main reason why these customers are checking up on you, or are there several reasons?

Mostly one reason, I guess. I get it in my head that they’re checking if I’m going to miss payments… because they keep asking about the new showroom. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but it doesn’t always feel that way to me.
Do you still believe that customers are checking up on you even when your husband or others try to reassure you that they're just being friendly?

Yes… sometimes I still do. Even when my husband says they’re just being friendly, I can get convinced they’re really coming in to check if I’ll miss payments, because they ask so many questions about the new showroom. It sounds odd, I know.
Do you believe that the voices you hear or the feelings you have about customers checking up on you are based on anything that's actually happening in real life?

I mean… partly, I guess. They really do ask a lot of questions about the new showroom. But then I get convinced it’s more than that, like they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, so… I don’t know. It still feels real to me sometimes.
Do you think the beliefs you have about customers checking up on you are something that you think about and believe in most of the time?

Not most of the time, no… but when they ask about the showroom, I can get stuck on it. I know it sounds odd, but then I start thinking they’re really checking if I’ll miss payments, even after my husband says they’re just being friendly.
Do you ever have times when you don't believe that customers are checking up on you?

Yes… there are times I don’t think that. When things are quiet, or nobody’s asking about the showroom, it doesn’t feel so real. But when they start asking too many questions, I can get convinced again, even if my husband says they’re just being friendly.
Do you believe that the idea of customers checking up on you is a strange or unrealistic thought that you have?

I guess… yes, I know it sounds odd. It’s just when customers ask too much about the new showroom, I start thinking they’re really checking whether I’ll miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, but sometimes I still get convinced.
